suggested_experiment_name: Bonati16 lattice QCD misalignment (Nf=2+1 topological susceptibility)
coupling_convention: y-values are the axion decay constant f_a in GeV (upper bound from misalignment producing the full DM abundance); x-values are the initial misalignment angle theta_0 in radians (linear axis), exactly as plotted
notes: Lattice QCD (Nf=2+1, physical quark masses) computation of the temperature dependence of the topological susceptibility, used to derive the axion misalignment dark matter abundance. Main phenomenological result: f_a(theta_0=2.2) = (1.00 +0.40/-0.26 +0.07/-0.18 +/- 0.06) x 10^12 GeV for the post-inflationary PQ breaking scenario, to be read as an upper bound on the PQ scale if axions constitute all of dark matter (or if topological defect contributions are non-negligible). This corresponds to m_a ~ 5.7 ueV. The result shifts the axion DM window by ~1 order of magnitude relative to dilute-instanton-gas estimates (f_a <~ 0.2e12 GeV). This is a cosmological bound on the f_a-m_a plane (AxionMass), not an experimental haloscope limit; no local DM density assumption applies (uses Omega_DM = 0.259 from Planck). Quoted uncertainties are fit/systematic errors, not a formal CL; the stated confidence_level is nominal.
